main_text.p: propter celerem caloris & spirituum fugam, aut sanguinis profusionem diffidamus de probationibus omni exceptione majoribus, quibus demonstretur, humores istos tres bilem, succum pancreaticum atque pituitam in intestino tenui effervescere, enimvero bilem humori acido permixtam cum eo effervescere docet Hippocrates de victu acutorum xxix. 8. 9. his expressis verbis etiam supra data occasione citatis, ubi inquit πὰ μὲν γαρ ἀπεφ' ἀλύεται ἢ ἐπιφλεγμαίνεται, μετεωρ-ζόμενα ἐπ' αὐτὲς videlicet ὀξεῖα ὀξύτητες: amara enim dissolvuntur & in pituitam transeunt, dum ab acido attolluntur, id est, effervescunt, quapropter quia Doctor Le Vasseur pag. 19. agnoscit succum pancreaticum acidum, uti & probatum supra p. 53. atque ipsa αὐτοψία constat succum pancreaticum in intestino duodeno bili permisceri, in homine enim utrumque ductum, tum pancreaticum tum bilarium intestinalem,

page.notes: Greek words in the italic line are only approximately rendered; the scan is small and partly blurred. Marked as doubtful: the Greek passage after "ubi inquit" and the word "αὐτοψία". The word "quapropter" and "quia" stand together in print with a missing space ("effervescunt,quapropter").
